synopsis: A useful virtual job site needs coordinated geometry, collision surfaces, ground mechanics and sensor-specific materials, not just convincing visuals; non-visual responses cannot be inferred from RGB textures, and camera, lidar and radar require wavelength-specific material data [f13113, f3713, f3715]. ASAM OpenMATERIAL 3D standardises assets and material properties for sensor-perception simulation: version 1.0.0 was released on 3 April 2025, while version 1.1.0 was planned for October 2026 but was not listed on the main page accessed that month [f7083, f3714, f3923, f3925]. Its coverage does not remove the need for separate environmental and contamination models, because weather and lighting are outside its stated scope and sensor soiling is explicitly excluded [f3919, f9372]. Radar credibility depends on material properties and the signal chain, with 77 GHz properties often requiring measurement; a 2025 wheel-loader study needed manual material tuning and reported detector failures partly attributable to guessed materials [f4418, f4420, f4421, f4423]. The booklet found no published job-site ultrasonic datasets, also reported missing thermal datasets, and recommends that the program measure or estimate material properties itself—a larger schedule item than computing power [f3943, f3717, f12951]. Site geometry and material libraries are proposed as work that can be completed before mid-2027, but acquiring and maintaining physically meaningful assets may consume more engineering effort than rendering them, and adapting road-centric material libraries to mines and quarries is non-trivial [f4973, f4966, f8462].
